idiom_name: class (or anonymous new Repository {}) over mutable.Map implementing the trait
implementation_notes: A Scala trait is the collaborator abstraction and the fake is a class - or an anonymous instantiation, new UserRepository { ... } - holding a mutable.Map, so the classic structure collapses into an ordinary declaration and no mocking framework is needed for working behaviour. Mocking libraries such as ScalaMock generate mocks with expectations, which serve the mock and stub rows. Keep the fake per-test (or clear the map), and prefer immutable case classes for the stored values so assertions compare by value.
pitfalls: mutable.Map is not thread-safe, and a fake defined in an object (Scala singleton) is shared across the suite - create it per test.
An anonymous instantiation captures the enclosing scope and cannot be inspected or reused; a named class is clearer once the fake grows.
Implicit parameters and path-dependent types make it easy to install a fake of the wrong instance; type the fake against the exact trait the code under test consumes.
